hypothesis: umpire strike zone is STRUCTURAL (like weather) rather than a participant attribute, so it should not be redundant with team form
method: cumulative prior-games-only averages, empirical-Bayes shrunk toward the season league mean with k=40 games, expressed as deviations

the_decisive_test.name: split-half reliability
the_decisive_test.method: split each umpire's games chronologically in half; if a real tendency exists, his first-half average must predict his second-half average
the_decisive_test.verdict: NO persistent tendency - the apparent effect is sampling noise

variance_decomposition.interpretation: umpire-to-umpire differences are only 12% larger than what random assignment of games would produce; essentially all apparent umpire 'personality' in run scoring is chance

why: Failed for a THIRD distinct reason. Prior rejections were redundancy (six families) and insufficient effect size (pitch matchup). This one is measurement unreliability: the underlying quantity does not persist, so there is nothing to measure. Correctly non-redundant and correctly computed, but the signal does not exist.
note: The raw correlation with total runs was NEGATIVE (-0.018), which is the signature of regression to the mean rather than a real tendency. That prompted the split-half test instead of accepting the number.
